newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares to trade sideways in 97 -Commerzbank.
newsitem.headline: German shares to trade sideways in 97 -Commerzbank.

text.p: Analysts at Commerzbank AG on Thursday forecast a sidewards move for Germany's DAX index for next year, with trading expected in a range between 2,500 and 2,850 points.
The bank said in its year-end brochure on the German stock market that the DAX had seen "superlative" growth in 1996, which would be difficult to beat in a climate of rising interest rates.

Commerzbank, Germany's third-largest bank, went on to say that there was room for further growth if current 13 percent profit growth projections for the 30 blue-chip German companies in the DAX index in 1998 turn out to be over-cautious.

Projected average profit growth in 1996 stood at 14 percent, rising to a possible 20 percent in 1997, Commerzbank said. The average price-earnings ratio, based on expectations for 1997, was 18, which Commerzbank said was a fair valuation.
The current low interest rate environment meant that the run of record highs which the DAX had seen over the course of the year were justified and secure.
Commerzbank was recommending the chemicals and the steel stock in particular.
"Commerzbank analysts have put industry stocks on their recommended list, which it thinks can profit from further improvement in the economic climate," Commerzbank said.

It said it was optmistic for engineering stocks in 1997, which will benefit from a pick-up in the western European economy, while electronics and technology stocks will continue to benefit from increased foreign orders.
German car-makers will see income improve slowly over 1997, and increased earnings and production will need to be accompanied by job cuts and limited pay hikes.

How the DAX-30 utility companies will fare depends on how the weather affects gas and electricity production, while the downwards trend in the construction sector will continue for the time being as demand in nearly all areas of construction is on the decrease.

The bank also recommends "second-line" stocks, which are heavily influenced by any upswing in the economy. Based on this outlook, Commerzbank is forecasting the MDAX index, which measures trade in seventy small-to-medium sized German companies, to increase 10 percent to 3,100 points in 1997.

Commerzbank is forecasting an end to what it called the "dream constellation" for German bonds seen in the second half of this year and forecasts a possible hike in key German interest rates expected around the middle of 1997.
